properties.foundation_analysis: Subterranean strata composed of Carboniferous sedimentary bedrock of the Inverclyde and Strathclyde Groups, overlain by dense glacial till. Structural masonry dominated by local Craigleith quartzitic sandstone (pale buff-grey, fine-grained, high-silica marine sandstone) alongside Hailes sandstone for structural bedding and foundational footings. Monument base incorporates polished Scottish red and grey granite courses bedded in high-calcium traditional non-hydraulic slaked lime mortar.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Urban parkland specimens of *Tilia × europaea* (Common Lime) and *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore). Phenological state for late December (winter dormancy): 100% complete defoliation, totally bare branch architecture revealing intricate ramification networks, dark wet bark crusted with dormant nitrophytic lichens (*Xanthoria parietina*), and dormant winter bud clusters.

properties.architectural_summary: Neoclassical urban ensemble centered on West Register House (former St George's Church, 1814, Robert Reid). Monumental central frontage features a tetrastyle Ionic portico with pediment, surmounted by an engaged attic stage, a peristyle drum with Corinthian colonnette pilasters, and a ribbed copper dome terminating in an ornate stone lantern. Flanking terraces comprise three-storey plus attic and rusticated basement Georgian townhouses (Robert Adam design, 1791). Elevations display rusticated ground-floor arcades with radial voussoirs, smooth ashlar upper levels ordered by giant-order pilasters, continuous string courses, moulded architraves, balustraded parapets, and timber 6-over-6 sash-and-case windows. In the central green, the Prince Albert Memorial (1876, John Steell) features a monumental bronze equestrian figure atop a stepped, multi-tiered granite pedestal with bronze bas-relief friezes.
